q: You set co-op campaign first, two players maximum. Can one person still play the whole campaign alone?
ctx: Follows your VIS-01 note. No bot partner (COOP-01), so a solo player has no partner for team moves; the story already has a solo traitor rule.

opts.label: Yes, fully solo
opts.desc: Every mission can be finished alone; team-move spots have a solo route; co-op is the main design target

opts.label: Solo, some routes shut
opts.desc: Missions can be finished alone, but some routes and secrets need two players

opts.label: Two players only
opts.desc: The campaign needs two players; solo is test-only

q: With two players maximum, the Mission 8 finale becomes one player against the other (the traitor). In solo, a computer-controlled traitor. Keep that?
ctx: Replaces STORY-02 (1v2 / 2v2 with three or four players). Story: the traitor is picked at random from the other player when Mission 8 loads; in solo, an operator the player did not pick.

opts.label: 1v1, AI in solo
opts.desc: Two players: one becomes the traitor; solo: a computer traitor

opts.label: Both vs AI traitor
opts.desc: Players never fight each other; the traitor is always a computer character

opts.label: Decide with finale
opts.desc: Decide when Mission 8 is written

q: The story has four operators (Wren, Moth, Tally, Sexton), but the game is now two players and only Wren and Moth are being built. What happens to Tally and Sexton?
ctx: Follows VIS-01 and ART-05. Tally owns Mission 6; Sexton has radio lines; every operator could be the traitor.

opts.label: Support crew on radio
opts.desc: They stay in the story as radio and briefing characters, not playable

opts.label: Four playable picks
opts.desc: Two players choose from four operators; Tally and Sexton get models later

opts.label: Cut them
opts.desc: Remove them from the story; rewrite their lines and Mission 6

q: You chose to delete the phone and touch code, the touch test, the old maps and the deathmatch / free-for-all / Wave code. Where should that deletion happen?
ctx: PLAT-01, PLAT-03, LEVEL-07, COOP-05. The consolidation plan allows merge fixes only, and deleting this much code makes the merge request hard to review.

opts.label: First job after merge
opts.desc: A clean-up branch straight after you merge this one; tests switch to desktop there (PLAT-02)

opts.label: In this merge
opts.desc: Do it now inside the consolidation, before the merge request opens

q: Hunter comes back later, but you deleted Wave, deathmatch and free-for-all and said no to team-versus-team. Keep the Hunter code parked until it returns?
ctx: VIS-03 (only Hunter returns), VIS-04 (no team vs team), COOP-05 (delete parked modes).

opts.label: Keep Hunter parked
opts.desc: Hunter code stays behind the hidden legacy switch; the other modes and the old Mission mode go

opts.label: Delete Hunter too
opts.desc: Rebuild it from scratch when it returns

q: Your note says stationary medkits in the map only. So no carried medkits: health comes back only at wall medkit stations, as in CT, and the hold-X heal goes. Right?
ctx: Follows CTRL-06. Today players carry 2 kits (3 on Rookie) and heal 40 over 1.5 s with X held; Proving has one wall station.

opts.label: Wall stations only
opts.desc: No carried kits, no kit count on the HUD; X hold freed; stations placed in every map

opts.label: Stations plus one kit
opts.desc: Wall stations, and each player also carries one kit

q: You want a stealth / kill selector next to the weapon wheel that locks your actions to that choice. What should it control?
ctx: Follows your CTRL-09 note (Blacklist-style selector). STEALTH-06: grab first, then finish, as in CT.

opts.label: All close actions
opts.desc: Grab finishes and takedowns knock out in Stealth and kill in Kill; tap / hold no longer chooses

opts.label: Grab finish only
opts.desc: Only the finish of a grab follows the selector; takedowns keep tap / hold

q: With the selector on Kill, what does the palm strike do?
ctx: The palm strike is a one-hit knockout from any side (M20). Follows FU-07.

opts.label: Still knocks out
opts.desc: The palm strike is always non-lethal; Kill only changes grabs and takedowns

opts.label: Becomes lethal
opts.desc: In Kill mode the strike kills

q: Three answers disagree on door bash: you removed the sprint bash, picked a door menu that lists 'bash', and kept 'a running push knocks out a guard behind the door'. Which?
ctx: MOVE-07 (remove door bashes), CTRL-05 (door pop-up list with bash), STEALTH-03 (run push knocks out).

opts.label: Bash from door menu
opts.desc: Bash is one choice in the door list; it can knock out a guard behind the door; running into a door does nothing special

opts.label: Running push bashes
opts.desc: Running into a door bashes it; the door list has open and stealth open only

opts.label: No bash at all
opts.desc: Doors open or stealth-open only

q: Heavies cannot be palm-struck. How can a player take a heavy out without shooting?
ctx: Follows your STEALTH-04 note (everyone except dogs and heavies).

opts.label: Grab from behind
opts.desc: Only a grab from behind, then knock out or kill

opts.label: Weapons and gadgets
opts.desc: No hand-to-hand at all; shoot or use gadgets

opts.label: Two players needed
opts.desc: A co-op double takedown only

q: You asked to review the 12-awake-characters limit for desktop. How should it be set?
ctx: Follows your STEALTH-09 note. The 12 came from phone budgets.

opts.label: Measure, then set
opts.desc: The performance job measures guards on the laptop and sets the cap; dogs and civilians count

opts.label: Raise to 20 now
opts.desc: 20 awake now; check on the laptop later

opts.label: Dogs, civilians free
opts.desc: Keep 12 guards; dogs and civilians do not count

q: You banned reference names everywhere. Does that also cover the reference game's title in our docs and your own quoted words in the decision files?
ctx: Follows VIS-06. Docs say 'modelled on Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory' and 'CT'; your decisions quote you saying 'pure chaos theory' and 'Sam'.

opts.label: Title ok, quotes kept
opts.desc: Characters, gear and organisations scrubbed; the game's title may name the reference in docs; your quotes stay word for word

opts.label: Scrub the title too
opts.desc: Docs say 'the reference game'; your quotes stay word for word

opts.label: Scrub everything
opts.desc: Title and names removed everywhere, your quotes included

q: You brought the tri-rotor drone back as a campaign gadget. When should it be built?
ctx: Follows ART-08. The drone is a parked gadget today; Wren's back pod is shaped for it.

opts.label: Gadget job, after slice
opts.desc: With the other gadgets after the vertical slice

opts.desc: Part of the Kestrel vertical slice

q: You chose to move the default button layout toward CT's. How far?
ctx: Follows CTRL-01 and CTRL-04 (back-to-wall on L3). Every button stays remappable.
